post.0:
I came third with 60. I won blue all three rounds and green in round III, but I never priced Cal's game-end cards: Snobs paid him 18 and Chronicler 7, which is more than any single contest, and I didn't see it coming because I was counting resources, not his blue bodies. The moment that cost me most was round III's opening: I bought Con Men with Spree, then Agents to block copies, and Encore copied Con Men's On Recruit anyway, so Cal and Ben each got their own steal-five (one via Echo of Encore) and Ben cashed 15 off it to run away. My Big Dilute into Makeover into all-green, then Doppelganger as Con Men to take five of Cal's blue, worked exactly as planned and won me 20 in the last round; it just came after Ben was already at 54 and I had no read on Cal's endgame. Next time I'd hate-draft Snobs in round II instead of leaving it for Cal.

META: The contest-holding versus spending tension is real and the rival-changing yellow spaces make every lead feel live, which is the best part of the game. What isn't working is that one On Recruit steal can be copied four or five times through Encore, Echo-of-Encore, Reprise and Doppelganger, and Agents doesn't stop it; Con Men decided round III for everyone. Second, game-end blue bodies (Snobs counting member counts, Chronicler) paid Cal 25 with almost no table visibility. The first thing I'd change: make Encore unable to copy a steal, or have Agents block member copies too.
post.1:
Lost to Cal by 3, 74 to 71. I led the whole game on efficiency: Guest Book refunds on cheap members, Busker, and two green copy chains won me yellow and green in rounds I and II. It was decided before I placed a minion in round III: Ava's Con Men and Cal's Encore copy each took 5 green off me, so my 10-green lead became Cal's 13. Without those 10 I hold green, and that's a 20-point swing. Then Snobs paid Cal +18 at game end because his 3-count blue bodies stack, and I never priced that in until it was too late to stop his yellow. My one mistake was a misclick on Dilute that turned one of Cal's yellow into blue instead of green. It didn't change the result.

META: Contests and 10-for-10 buying make a clean numbers game, and Yellow's Dilute and Harvest give it real fights. The two things that went wrong are copyable steals and member-count game-end scoring: Con Men through Green's copies took 15 resources off the table in round III, and Snobs counting 3-count bodies paid Cal 18. First fix: make Con Men's On Recruit uncopyable (or have Encore skip steals), then look at Snobs counting member count instead of cards.
post.2:
I won 74 to Ben's 71, and honestly Ben outplayed me on contests and follower buys for two rounds; I was 27 to his 54 early in round III. Two things won it: stealing Ben's yellow with Reprise into my own Encore of Ava's Con Men, then taking both Melting Pot and Trade Seeds so Ben had no yellow space left on the last turn, worth +10. The other was Snobs paying +18 at the end, because Trendsetters, Window Dressers, Drifters (picked as blue), Connoisseurs and Doormen all count as 2 or 3 blue members. I paid 6 for Snobs in round II without realizing member counts multiply it, so that win was half luck. I also fumbled one Big Dilute copy by misclicking and flipping Ava's resources back and forth, which cost me a blue lead in round II.

META: The contest races and the copy chains make for real dilemmas, and the last few turns of round III were tense and readable. What isn't working: one-time On Recruit steals become repeatable through Encore, Echo, Reprise and Doppelganger, and Agents doesn't stop any of it, so Con Men decided too much. Member-count bodies multiplying the per-member end bonuses (Snobs +18) swing the game too much. I'd fix first: Encore and Doppelganger shouldn't copy steals, or Con Men's steal should only fire for its owner.
